chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Everything is to be referred back to the Book and the Sunnah, and every hadith that is not in accordance with the Book of God is mere ornamentation (falsehood).'

key_terms.الْكِتَابُ وَالسُّنَّةُ: The Book (Quran) and the Sunnah (prophetic practice) — the two primary sources of Islamic law and doctrine
key_terms.زُخْرُفٌ: Zukhruf — literally 'ornamentation' or gilded falsehood; used in Quran 6:112 for deceptive speech and 43:35 for worldly adornment
key_terms.مَرْدُودٌ: Referred back / rejected — the principle of returning disputed matters to the foundational sources

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about hadiths that contradict the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a foundational principle of hadith criticism: the Quran and Sunnah together constitute the supreme criterion for evaluating all narrations. Any hadith that contradicts the Book of God is to be rejected as 'zukhruf' — literally 'ornamentation' or decoration, a Quranic term (6:112, 43:35) implying false glitter with no substance. This teaching was directed to early Shia scholars who needed reliable criteria to distinguish authentic transmissions from fabrications circulating in an era of political upheaval and sectarian rivalries.
